sources.excerpt: Jane Eyre is a novel by the English writer Charlotte Brontë.
Madame Bovary: Provincial Manners, commonly known as simply Madame Bovary, is the début novel of French writer Gustave Flaubert, originally published in 1856 and 1857.
Anna Karenina is a novel, first published in book form in 1878, by the Russian author Leo Tolstoy.
The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark, often shortened to Hamlet, is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare sometime between 1599 and 1601.
William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet and actor.
Tartuffe, or The Impostor, or The Hypocrite, first performed in 1664, is a theatrical comedy by Molière.
Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, known by his stage name Molière, was a French playwright, actor, and poet, widely regarded as one of the great writers in the French language and world literature.
The Seagull is a play by Russian dramatist Anton Chekhov, written in 1895 and first produced in 1896.
"Ozymandias" is a sonnet written by the English Romantic poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, first published in the 11 January 1818 issue of The Examiner of London.
Le Bateau ivre is a Symbolist poem written in the summer of 1871 by French poet Arthur Rimbaud, then aged sixteen.
Widely considered to be Pushkin's most successful narrative poem, The Bronze Horseman has had a lasting impact on Russian literature.
Alexander Sergeyevich Pushkin was a Russian poet, playwright, and novelist of the Romantic era.
